scope: Only the added single test, PrivatePgRoute, factory overload, exact candidate artifacts, and narrowly necessary referenced methods.

findings.title: Initial dispatcher retains the direct materializer
findings.detail: The added case constructs routedMaterialization with routedJdbc at line 625 and passes it to the session factory at line 643, but constructs the initial GuidedDispatchService with the autowired materialization field. That field is created by Application.materialization(actualJdbc), so this participant owns the direct DataSource rather than routedSource. The recovery dispatcher correctly uses routedMaterialization at line 809. The initial service graph therefore does not satisfy the explicitly required SAME DataSource instance for every participant.
findings.impact: The candidate construction audit omits this direct materializer and cannot substantiate its complete graph claim. Narrow reference inspection shows that this dispatcher currently invokes only materialization.identity, which performs contract validation without JDBC, so this finding does not assert an observed SQL bypass or invalidate the genuineness of the routed transaction-begin failure. The test can nevertheless pass with the required graph invariant violated.
findings.requestedCorrection: Use routedMaterialization in the added case's initial dispatcher and include both initial and recovered dispatchers in the frozen construction audit. Preserve the original parameterized case.

findings.title: A failed proxy reopen skips caller interruption and join
findings.detail: The finally block calls route.reopen() before interrupting and joining the caller, in the same try block. PrivatePgRoute.reopen() can throw IOException from same-port server.bind at line 901. If that happens while the original caller is still waiting for the partial HTTPS response, control jumps to the cleanup catch and never executes lines 850-852. The remaining finally only clears the captured buffers, and closing PrivatePgRoute closes JDBC sockets rather than the caller's HTTPS exchange.
findings.impact: On this cleanup failure path the test exits without even attempting to interrupt or reap the caller. The caller, relay response loop, and relay-owned receive buffer can outlive the case until unrelated transport or class teardown occurs. Suppressing the reopen error preserves the assertion failure but does not establish the claimed bounded cleanup; forced clearing of captured buffers can also occur while their owner is still running.
findings.requestedCorrection: Make proxy restoration and caller interruption/join independent cleanup attempts, always attempting bounded caller cleanup even when restoration fails. Preserve the primary failure and attach cleanup failures. Keep any associated socket/executor cleanup exception-safe without introducing a production deadline claim.

findings.title: Cancellation's asynchronous stop can race proxy closure
findings.detail: The restarted service installs recovered::stop at line 813. Its public cancel commits the terminal rows and schedules a CompletableFuture.runAsync stop sender plus a routed repository transaction to persist teardownStatus=CONFIRMED. The new test checks CANCELLED, UNKNOWN_OUTCOME, and terminal USAGE, then immediately leaves the case; the outer resource close can cut the routed sockets while that asynchronous task is still sending or opening/using its confirmation transaction. None of those terminal-row assertions waits for this task, and the PrivatePgRoute executor does not own or join the common-pool task.
findings.impact: Even a passing run can leave cancellation teardown work running beyond the case or cause its confirmation transaction to fail because the test itself closes the restored route. The test establishes an authorized terminal database transition, but not bounded completion of the separate closure it initiates. It also does not assert that materialization.live becomes false after cancellation.
findings.requestedCorrection: Keep the restored route alive through a bounded, observable completion check for the separate authorized stop/confirmation and verify materialization closure. Ensure failure-path cleanup accounts for that initiated work before proxy destruction. Do not attribute these later commits to the failed lost-acknowledgment helper.

A new-key historical command row is permitted by the referenced AlreadyConsumed implementation; it does not grant another send.
